Galarza26RelativeCredit.crossingConditio.declaration_source:
/-- Mathematical content of Assumption 4, including the two strict
interiority conditions at the compared price for every opacity. -/
def crossingConditions (qbar Rbar E D0 : ℝ)
    (a g c : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn a (Icc 0 1) ∧ ContinuousOn g (Icc 0 1) ∧
  ContinuousOn c (Icc 0 1) ∧
  (∀ k ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, 0 < a k ∧ 0 < g k ∧ 0 < c k) ∧
  StrictAntiOn (fun k ↦ screeningAdvantage (a k) (g k) (c k)) (Icc 0 1) ∧
  0 < screeningAdvantage (a 0) (g 0) (c 0) ∧
  screeningAdvantage (a 1) (g 1) (c 1) < 0 ∧
  (∀ k ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, interiorRegime qbar (a k) (g k) (c k) Rbar E D0)

  ContinuousOn a (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
    ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
      ContinuousOn c (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
        (∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, 0 < a k ∧ 0 < g k ∧ 0 < c k) ∧
          StrictAntiOn (fun (k : ℝ) => Galarza26RelativeCredit.screeningAdvantage (a k) (g k) (c k)) (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
            0 < Galarza26RelativeCredit.screeningAdvantage (a 0) (g 0) (c 0) ∧
              Galarza26RelativeCredit.screeningAdvantage (a 1) (g 1) (c 1) < 0 ∧
                ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, Galarza26RelativeCredit.interiorRegime qbar (a k) (g k) (c k) Rbar E D0

Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice.declaration_source:
/-- The paper's simple, unweighted peer comparison.  The peer vector has
`n + 3` entries, so the empirical minimum of three other banks is built into
the carrier and the evaluated bank is supplied separately. -/
def relativePrice {n : ℕ} (ownRate baseRate : ℝ)
    (peerRates : Fin (n + 3) → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (ownRate - baseRate) -
    (∑ k, (peerRates k - baseRate)) / (Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)) : ℝ)
Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice.semantic_target:
type:
{n : ℕ} → ℝ → ℝ → (Fin (n + 3) → ℝ) → ℝ

value:
fun {n : ℕ} (ownRate baseRate : ℝ) (peerRates : Fin (n + 3) → ℝ) =>
  ownRate - baseRate - (∑ k : Fin (n + 3), (peerRates k - baseRate)) / ↑(Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)))

Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice_eq.declaration_source:
/-- Algebraic cancellation of the common base in the paper's equation (1). -/
theorem relativePrice_eq_rate_gap {n : ℕ} (ownRate baseRate : ℝ)
    (peerRates : Fin (n + 3) → ℝ) :
    relativePrice ownRate baseRate peerRates =
      ownRate - (∑ k, peerRates k) / (Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)) : ℝ) := by
  have hcard : (Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)) : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    simp only [Fintype.card_fin, ne_eq]
    positivity
  simp only [relativePrice, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const,
    Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul, Fintype.card_fin]
  field_simp
  ring
Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice_eq.semantic_target:
∀ {n : ℕ} (ownRate baseRate : ℝ) (peerRates : Fin (n + 3) → ℝ),
  Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice ownRate baseRate peerRates =
    ownRate - (∑ k : Fin (n + 3), peerRates k) / ↑(Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)))

governing_continuation_model.verbatim_source_input:
Ambiente y decisión del banco

4.1.

Agentes, información, unidades y cronología

El único agente que optimiza en este modelo es un banco neutral al riesgo. Los solicitantes
y los bancos pares determinan una calidad y una referencia reducidas; no se modela su juego
estratégico. El supervisor observa D y más tarde un ratio de cartera, pero no el esfuerzo ni toda la
composición de riesgo. La opacidad κ ∈ [0, 1] es una característica exógena del segmento: un valor
mayor representa menor información veriﬁcable inicial. No se estima este índice ni se equipara
automáticamente microempresa con opacidad alta.
La cronología es: primero se ﬁjan segmento, tecnología y precio observado; después se forma el
conjunto de solicitantes y el banco observa su riesgo medio; luego elige esfuerzo antes de originar;
ﬁnalmente se realiza el estado crediticio y se observa la cartera al horizonte h. El banco conoce los
parámetros al decidir. La incertidumbre de desempeño permanece y se integra en su objetivo. El
precio es un argumento del problema de continuación, no una variable resuelta en equilibrio.
q 0 y q son probabilidades sin unidades, referidas al mismo evento y horizonte para una cohorte
estandarizada. e y κ son índices. D se mide en unidades de tasa anual decimal. Los pagos y costos
se normalizan por sol de crédito. La sensibilidad monetaria del premio de desempeño a una unidad
de D se normaliza a uno. Esto es una simpliﬁcación de remuneración, no una conversión exacta de
tasas efectivas a cualquier plazo contractual.

Galarza26RelativeCredit.conditionedPayof.declaration_source:
/-- The positive performance premium in Assumption 3 on the admissible domain.
The objective and feasible set themselves are `bankProfit` and
`feasibleEfforts`; their explicit arguments keep price fixed during an effort
comparison. -/
def conditionedPayoff (Rbar lower upper : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ D ∈ Icc lower upper, 0 < premium Rbar D

ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → Prop

Galarza26RelativeCredit.crossingConditio.declaration_source:
/-- Mathematical content of Assumption 4, including the two strict
interiority conditions at the compared price for every opacity. -/
def crossingConditions (qbar Rbar E D0 : ℝ)
    (a g c : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn a (Icc 0 1) ∧ ContinuousOn g (Icc 0 1) ∧
  ContinuousOn c (Icc 0 1) ∧
  (∀ k ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, 0 < a k ∧ 0 < g k ∧ 0 < c k) ∧
  StrictAntiOn (fun k ↦ screeningAdvantage (a k) (g k) (c k)) (Icc 0 1) ∧
  0 < screeningAdvantage (a 0) (g 0) (c 0) ∧
  screeningAdvantage (a 1) (g 1) (c 1) < 0 ∧
  (∀ k ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, interiorRegime qbar (a k) (g k) (c k) Rbar E D0)
Galarza26RelativeCredit.crossingConditio.semantic_target:
type:
ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → (ℝ → ℝ) → (ℝ → ℝ) → (ℝ → ℝ) → Prop

value:
fun (qbar Rbar E D0 : ℝ) (a g c : ℝ → ℝ) =>
  ContinuousOn a (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
    ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
      ContinuousOn c (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
        (∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, 0 < a k ∧ 0 < g k ∧ 0 < c k) ∧
          StrictAntiOn (fun (k : ℝ) => Galarza26RelativeCredit.screeningAdvantage (a k) (g k) (c k)) (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
            0 < Galarza26RelativeCredit.screeningAdvantage (a 0) (g 0) (c 0) ∧
              Galarza26RelativeCredit.screeningAdvantage (a 1) (g 1) (c 1) < 0 ∧
                ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, Galarza26RelativeCredit.interiorRegime qbar (a k) (g k) (c k) Rbar E D0

Galarza26RelativeCredit.feasibleEfforts.semantic_target:
type:
ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → Prop

Galarza26RelativeCredit.floorRegime.declaration_source:
/-- The strict probability-floor regime used in the third line of (4). -/
def floorRegime (qbar a g c Rbar E D : ℝ) : Prop :=
  priorRisk qbar a D / g < g * premium Rbar D / c ∧
    priorRisk qbar a D / g < E
Galarza26RelativeCredit.floorRegime.semantic_target:
type:
ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → Prop

value:
fun (qbar a g c Rbar E D : ℝ) =>
  Galarza26RelativeCredit.priorRisk qbar a D / g < g * Galarza26RelativeCredit.premium Rbar D / c ∧
    Galarza26RelativeCredit.priorRisk qbar a D / g < E

Galarza26RelativeCredit.impairedBalance.semantic_target:

ℝ → ℝ → (ℝ → ℝ) → (ℝ → ℝ) → ℝ → ℝ

Galarza26RelativeCredit.interiorRegime.declaration_source:
/-- The two strict interior inequalities used in the first line of (4). -/
def interiorRegime (qbar a g c Rbar E D : ℝ) : Prop :=
  g * premium Rbar D / c < E ∧
    g * premium Rbar D / c < priorRisk qbar a D / g
Galarza26RelativeCredit.interiorRegime.semantic_target:
type:
ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → Prop

value:
fun (qbar a g c Rbar E D : ℝ) =>
  g * Galarza26RelativeCredit.premium Rbar D / c < E ∧
    g * Galarza26RelativeCredit.premium Rbar D / c < Galarza26RelativeCredit.priorRisk qbar a D / g

type:
ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

value:
fun (qbar a g c Rbar E D : ℝ) =>
  min (g * Galarza26RelativeCredit.premium Rbar D / c) (min E (Galarza26RelativeCredit.priorRisk qbar a D / g))

Galarza26RelativeCredit.optimalRisk.semantic_target:
type:
ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ

value:

/-- Performance premium; paper S3. -/
def premium (Rbar D : ℝ) : ℝ := Rbar + D

Galarza26RelativeCredit.priorRisk.declaration_source:

def priorRisk (qbar a D : ℝ) : ℝ := qbar + a * D

Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice.declaration_source:
/-- The paper's simple, unweighted peer comparison.  The peer vector has
`n + 3` entries, so the empirical minimum of three other banks is built into
the carrier and the evaluated bank is supplied separately. -/
def relativePrice {n : ℕ} (ownRate baseRate : ℝ)
    (peerRates : Fin (n + 3) → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (ownRate - baseRate) -
    (∑ k, (peerRates k - baseRate)) / (Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)) : ℝ)
Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice.semantic_target:
type:
{n : ℕ} → ℝ → ℝ → (Fin (n + 3) → ℝ) → ℝ

value:
fun {n : ℕ} (ownRate baseRate : ℝ) (peerRates : Fin (n + 3) → ℝ) =>
  ownRate - baseRate - (∑ k : Fin (n + 3), (peerRates k - baseRate)) / ↑(Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)))

Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice_eq.declaration_source:
/-- Algebraic cancellation of the common base in the paper's equation (1). -/
theorem relativePrice_eq_rate_gap {n : ℕ} (ownRate baseRate : ℝ)
    (peerRates : Fin (n + 3) → ℝ) :
    relativePrice ownRate baseRate peerRates =
      ownRate - (∑ k, peerRates k) / (Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)) : ℝ) := by
  have hcard : (Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)) : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    simp only [Fintype.card_fin, ne_eq]
    positivity
  simp only [relativePrice, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const,
    Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul, Fintype.card_fin]
  field_simp
  ring
Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice_eq.semantic_target:
∀ {n : ℕ} (ownRate baseRate : ℝ) (peerRates : Fin (n + 3) → ℝ),
  Galarza26RelativeCredit.relativePrice ownRate baseRate peerRates =
    ownRate - (∑ k : Fin (n + 3), peerRates k) / ↑(Fintype.card (Fin (n + 3)))

Galarza26RelativeCredit.screenedRisk.declaration_source:

Galarza26RelativeCredit.selectionAndDoma.declaration_source:
/-- Mathematical content of Assumption 1 on one compact price interval. -/
def selectionAndDomain (qbar a lower upper : ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 < qbar ∧ qbar < 1 ∧ 0 < a ∧ lower ≤ upper ∧
    ∀ D ∈ Icc lower upper, priorRisk qbar a D ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1
Galarza26RelativeCredit.selectionAndDoma.semantic_target:
type:
ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → Prop

value:
fun (qbar a lower upper : ℝ) =>
  0 < qbar ∧
    qbar < 1 ∧
      0 < a ∧ lower ≤ upper ∧ ∀ D ∈ Set.Icc lower upper, Galarza26RelativeCredit.priorRisk qbar a D ∈ Set.Icc 0 1

Galarza26RelativeCredit.stockAccountingC.declaration_source:
/-- Quantitative part of Assumption 5.  The ledger declarations above encode
the deterministic/continuous-population accounting convention and the absence
of an additional risk-selection or write-off term. -/
def stockAccountingConditions (B0 m0 lower upper : ℝ) (B : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 < B0 ∧ m0 ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
    (∀ D ∈ Icc lower upper, 0 < B D ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ B D)
Galarza26RelativeCredit.stockAccountingC.semantic_target:
type:
ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → (ℝ → ℝ) → Prop

value:
fun (B0 m0 lower upper : ℝ) (B : ℝ → ℝ) =>
  0 < B0 ∧ m0 ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧ ∀ D ∈ Set.Icc lower upper, 0 < B D ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ B D

Galarza26RelativeCredit.technologyCapaci.declaration_source:
/-- Mathematical content of Assumption 2.  Real-valued Lean parameters are
finite; positivity and the nonnegative capacity are the material restrictions. -/
def technologyCapacityCost (g c E : ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 < g ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 ≤ E
